Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP) has launched its Credit Opportunities Fund (COF), expanding its private credit platform with a strategy that complements its existing Green Credit Fund (GCF). The fund focuses on OECD markets and targets opportunities requiring specialist expertise in structuring flexible capital solutions and assessing technical, engineering, construction and operational risks.

The fund has a target size of USD 1 billion and is supported by anchor investors and a commitment from CIP.

COF has completed its initial seed close and made its first investment, providing financing for a thermal energy storage and industrial decarbonisation project in Kansas, USA. The project involves a thermal battery with a capacity of 5.8 GWh.

Its investments will cover sectors in which CIP has established investment strategies or in-house technical and operational expertise. These include clean power and grid infrastructure, low-carbon fuels and carbon management, and the circular economy.

COF provides structured and flexible capital across the energy infrastructure value chain, while GCF primarily provides senior secured debt to renewable energy and storage companies.
